chunk_findings.detail: The change documents the escape hatch for a large diff as `--delta` in both user-facing places — the config docstring ("`--delta` asks for one delta whatever the default (for a very large diff)") and the driver template ("`--delta` sends only the commits since the reviewed head") — while the stated intent for this change says delta-only "remains available, with `--delta-only`". Both cannot be true: either the CLI flag is `--delta-only` and every operator who follows these two documents types `--delta` and gets an "unknown option" error exactly when the diff is too large for a full re-review (the one case the flag exists for), or the flag is `--delta` and the change description is wrong. Since the new docs are the only guidance for the newly-introduced `--delta` path, the flag name must be made to match the implemented parser before this ships.

chunk_findings.detail: The help text and driver doc advertise the delta-only escape hatch as `--delta` ("`--delta` reviews only the commits since the head that review covered"), while the change's own stated design names that flag `--delta-only` ("Delta-only remains available, with `--delta-only`, for very large diffs"). A user who follows the new help text and runs `ddflow review <ID> --gate G --delta` on a diff too large to send twice will hit an unknown/unsupported option (or select nothing) instead of the delta-only round the design says exists. The `mcp_instructions.md` edit compounds this by exposing the same mode as `delta=true` without the tool side ever being described as `--delta`; whichever of the two names is authoritative, one of the three edited documents is now wrong about the user-facing interface.

chunk_findings.detail: `prior` is the value produced by `_announce_rerun(rerun, revs, item, gate, say)` on the line above, and it is the same variable the delta path uses to "merge into the record" the findings of the earlier review — i.e. it is truthy exactly when a previous review of this gate exists. The guard at the top of `_with_previous_findings` is `if kind != "full" or rerun or it is None: return context`, so passing `prior` there short-circuits precisely in the situation the function was written for: a full re-review of an item that already has gate findings. Concretely, re-run `ddflow review` on an item whose gate already recorded findings (`kind == "full"`, `_last_review(...)["chunk_findings"]` non-empty, triage present, `it` not None); the `or rerun` branch fires because `prior` is truthy/non-empty, `_with_previous_findings` returns the original `context`, and the reviewer is never shown the previous findings or their triage. That defeats the stated intent (D-gate-economy 3: a re-review must send the whole diff plus the previous findings), so the new code is effectively dead for every re-review. Note the actual rerun flag (`rerun`, the enclosing argument already in scope) is not what is being passed here; the guard should be fed that flag, or `_with_previous_findings` should not treat "a previous review exists" as "this is a chunk re-run".
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:1154 — `_with_previous_findings(..., rerun=prior)`

chunk_findings.detail: The change describes the escape hatch as `--delta-only` ("Delta-only remains available, with --delta-only, for very large diffs"), but both doc surfaces added here call it `--delta`: the config doc says "`--delta` asks for one delta whatever the default (for a very large diff)" and the template says "`--delta` sends only the commits since the reviewed head ... for a diff too large to send twice". These parentheticals ("for a very large diff" / "for a diff too large") identify the same flag the intent names `--delta-only`, so one of the two names is wrong. If the CLI option is `--delta-only` (as the intent states), then a user following the documented plain re-review workflow on a large diff runs `ddflow review <ID> --gate G --delta`, which the argument parser rejects as an unknown option, and no delta is produced; if instead the option really is `--delta`, the intent's naming is wrong and the operator/agent instructions shipped in the template point at a flag that does not exist. Either way the reviewed text and the stated feature disagree on the user-visible CLI surface, so at least one of these two documented invocations is unusable.

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten help text tells the operator that a delta re-review is requested with `ddflow review <id> --gate G --delta` ("`--delta` reviews only the commits since the head that review covered"), and the driver doc repeats it ("`--delta` sends only the commits since the reviewed head"). This change's own specification names that flag `--delta-only`: "Delta-only remains available, with `--delta-only`, for very large diffs." If the CLI registers `--delta-only` (as specified) and not `--delta`, then the exact scenario this text exists for — a diff too large to send twice — is the one where following the help text fails: `ddflow review <id> --gate G --delta` exits with an unrecognized-argument error, and the operator has no delta escape hatch from the newly-full default round. Either both docs must say `--delta-only`, or the spec's flag name is wrong; as written the shipped help text documents a flag the change was not specified to add.

data.body:
For a diff under [review].combined_under_lines (default 150), ddflow review --gate rubber_duck,critic sends ONE request whose prompt covers both lenses and records the outcome for both gates, with the shared review id in evidence. Larger diffs keep both reviews, run in parallel. The round limit (max_rounds 2) also bounds delta rounds. After it, the gate is passed-on-refutation (flagged, D-unify 5) when every finding has a probe, or escalated to the operator.

Split into: B-gate-econ-review-combined, B-gate-econ-review-budget, B-gate-econ-review-refutation.

The one-gate review is unchanged and reused for both paths; diff measurement reuses diff_for/commit_diff.

chunk_findings.detail: `_any_out_of_rounds` is called only with `asked[1:]`, so the first gate's budget is never consulted when choosing the combined path. Input: `gate="rubber_duck,critic"`, a diff with `0 < lines < under`, rubber_duck already at its round limit and critic still in budget. `_any_out_of_rounds(..., ["critic"], ...)` returns False, so `_review_combined` runs and calls `_review_gate(gate="rubber_duck")`; that call is refused on budget, so `st.items[item].gates["rubber_duck"].evidence["review_id"] != rid` and the `for g in asked[1:]` loop is skipped entirely. The requested `critic` review is then neither run nor recorded (the returned outcome is just rubber_duck's refusal), even though critic had budget. The docstring's own contract — that out-of-rounds gates are refused "on its own" while the others still run — only holds when the gate lacking budget is not the first one; excluding `asked[0]` from the check silently drops every later gate whenever the first gate is exhausted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py `_review_gates` / `_any_out_of_rounds` (`asked[1:]`)

chunk_findings.detail: The filter distinguishes file-header lines from content lines purely by prefix, but a content line can itself begin with `+`/`-`. Input: a diff that adds the C/JS line `++counter;` — the emitted diff line is `+` + `++counter;` = `+++counter;`, which is discarded as if it were a `+++ b/file` header; likewise removing a line `-- counter` or a SQL/Ada/Haskell comment `-- note` yields `---note`, discarded as a `--- a/file` header. Each such line is subtracted twice from `lines`, so the count is wrong; e.g. with `combined_under_lines = 5` and exactly 5 changed lines one of which is `-- note`, `lines` computes 4 and the code takes `_review_combined` (one shared review) where the true count would have selected `_review_parallel` (one review per gate), which is the behaviour the threshold exists to control.

chunk_findings.detail: The docstring promises "one reviewer request whose intent names every gate's lens", but the appended instruction hardcodes the two lens names: "(rubber_duck)" for refutation and "(critic)" for criticism, regardless of `asked`. The function is reached for any comma-separated gate list from the CLI (gate names come from `GD.load_gates`), so for input `gate="rubber_duck,arbiter"` the single request tells the reviewer to apply rubber_duck's and critic's lenses and never describes `arbiter`'s, and the same (possibly wrong) text is recorded as the evidence/intent for both gates' records in the `for g in asked[1:]` loop. The combined review is recorded for every requested gate while only ever instructing the two hardcoded lenses.

chunk_findings.detail: The out-of-rounds probe deliberately skips the first gate, so the first gate's exhausted budget does not trigger the per-gate fallback — yet the combined review *is* recorded under that first gate, so the first gate's refusal poisons the whole call. Concretely: `combined_under_lines = 200`, a diff of 5 changed lines, an item where `rubber_duck` has already used its last round and `critic` has full budget, and `--gate rubber_duck,critic`. `lines = 5` satisfies `0 < 5 < 200`, and `_any_out_of_rounds(log, cfg, item, ["critic"], args)` is `False` because only `asked[1:]` is inspected, so `_review_combined` is taken. Inside, `_review_gate(gate="rubber_duck", ...)` refuses (out of rounds) and therefore records nothing, so `rec = st.items[item].gates.get("rubber_duck")` is the *previous* record and `rec.evidence.get("review_id") == rid` is false; the `if` body is skipped and `critic` is never invoked at all — the caller gets only rubber_duck's refusal. The docstring of `_review_gates` promises the opposite for exhausted gates ("then each gate runs, and is refused, on its own"), and the dispatcher docstring promises "one review per gate" whenever the combined path is not taken. If instead `_review_gate` records refusals, the second branch of the bug appears: because the refusal record carries the shared `review_id`, `asked[1:]` are then recorded with the *refusal* outcome, marking `critic` as exhausted/refused even though it had budget. Either way `critic` is not reviewed as promised. The condition needs to consider every gate in `asked` (i.e. `asked`, not `asked[1:]`), so that an exhausted first gate falls through to `_review_parallel` and the remaining gates still run.

chunk_findings.detail:
The new paragraph states the fallback for a big diff: "A larger change runs one review per gate, one after the other." That directly contradicts the stated intent of the change, which is that "larger diffs run both reviews in parallel." Concretely, for `ddflow review T1 --gate rubber_duck,critic` on a diff of, say, 200 changed lines (≥ `review.combined_under_lines`, so the combined path is not taken), the reviewed behavior is two reviewer requests issued concurrently, while the README just added tells the user the two reviews happen sequentially ("one after the other"). A user reasoning about the documented contract — e.g. assuming only one reviewer agent is ever live at a time, or reasoning about ordering of the two gates' outputs — is misled by the text shipped in this diff. Either the README should say the two reviews run in parallel, or the intent/implementation is wrong and the diff's fallback is actually sequential; as given, the doc and the described behavior cannot both be true.

(Note for the earlier HIGH finding on `_review_gates` / `_any_out_of_rounds`: the same paragraph now documents that "a pair where either gate is out of rounds" runs per gate rather than combined, which is the behavior that finding asked for, so it is not re-raised here.)

chunk_findings.detail:
The diff changes the call site to `_any_out_of_rounds(log, cfg, item, asked, args)` and the probe function now iterates `for g in gates`, so the first gate is no longer skipped. That part of the prior finding is addressed, but the guard still does not fire, and the author's own probe records the exact bad outcome ("rubber_duck at max_rounds, critic in budget: the combined path ran and critic was never reviewed").

The remaining defect is the round count handed to `_budget`. `_any_out_of_rounds` passes `_full_rounds(log, item, g)` — the number of full rounds *already completed*. But the review it is trying to authorize is the *next* full round; the same diff computes that prospective round as `done + 1` in `_rounds_for` (`"round": done + 1`). So when `rubber_duck` has consumed exactly its `max_rounds` (i.e. `_full_rounds == max_rounds`), `_budget(cfg, item, "rubber_duck", max_rounds, ...)` does not flag it (the actual refusal is for the `max_rounds + 1`-th round), `_any_out_of_rounds` returns `False`, and `_review_combined` is entered.

Concrete failure: `[review].combined_under_lines = 200`, a diff with 5 changed lines, `--gate rubber_duck,critic`, an item where `rubber_duck` is at its last round and `critic` is in budget. `lines = 5` satisfies `0 < 5 < 200`; `_any_out_of_rounds` checks `rubber_duck` with `_full_rounds = max_rounds`, sees no refusal, and returns `False`, so the combined path runs. Inside it, `_review_gate(gate="rubber_duck", full=True)` performs the real (prospective) budget check, refuses, and returns `unavailable`; the `elif item and out.data.get("outcome") == "unavailable"` branch then records `critic = unavailable` via `GD.record` without ever reviewing it. The fix (replacing `asked[1:]` with `asked`) is necessary but not sufficient: the argument passed to `_budget` must be the round being authorized (`_full_rounds(...) + 1`), otherwise the gate sitting at the limit is still judged in budget and poisons the whole combined call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py `_any_out_of_rounds` (the `_budget(...)` argument)

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier finding still holds, by the author's own triage. The triage line reads `confirmed -- probe: rubber_duck at max_rounds, critic in budget: the combined path ran and critic was never reviewed`. A probe that answers a *fixed* finding would have to show the opposite result — that with one gate exhausted the combined path is suppressed and the still-in-budget gate is reviewed on its own. Instead the probe records exactly the failure the finding describes: `--gate rubber_duck,critic` on a diff smaller than `combined_under_lines`, with `rubber_duck` at `max_rounds` and `critic` in budget, runs the combined request and `critic` is never reviewed. That is what happens when the out-of-rounds check still skips the first gate (`asked[1:]`): the combined review is recorded under the first gate, the first gate's refusal poisons the shared call, and the second gate loses its round without ever being reviewed. The fix (consulting all requested gates, including the first, before taking the combined path) is not present in this part, and the probe does not demonstrate it, so the defect remains.

chunk_findings.detail: The `on_exceed` description in this hunk was rewritten to drop `--delta` from the refusal message ("exit 3, naming `review triage`, `--force --reason` and how to change the cap"), but the sentence immediately after it is left untouched: *"A delta recheck and triage are never refused either way."* Given the stated intent — "`[review].max_rounds` bounds delta rounds too: a delta after the cap is refused like a full round" — the delta half of that sentence is now false. Concrete case: with `max_rounds = 2`, two rounds recorded, `on_exceed = refuse`, a user (or an agent reading this doc through `ddflow_configure`) runs `ddflow review <id> --gate rubber_duck --delta`; the run exits 3, yet the documented contract says a delta "is never refused either way". The line was already being modified in this diff, so the stale clause is not an oversight of scope — it directly contradicts the neighboring `max_rounds` text and the new `--delta` help in the same change. (The `review triage` half of the sentence is still correct; only the "delta recheck ... never refused" claim is wrong.)

chunk_findings.detail: The test writes `x = 3  # FINDME` and commits it, then asserts the delta review exits `OK`. The fake reviewer in this suite treats `# FINDME` as a finding: the adjacent test relies on triage finding index `1` after reviewing the same fixture, so the delta prompt containing the changed `+x = 3  # FINDME` line will make the reviewer return `FAIL`, not `OK`. The assertion should accept `in (OK, FAIL)` or expect `FAIL`; as written, the test fails or incorrectly masks the reviewer's finding.
